press: Chest pressing involves shoulder movement and elbow extension.
Practise moving the load away from the chest while keeping a stable support position.
Choose a light resistance and a range you can lower without losing your setup.
fly: Reference establishes chest-training anatomy; the fly variation requires separate trainer verification.
Trains bringing the upper arms across the torso with limited elbow movement.
Start with a short, comfortable arc and light resistance; a deeper stretch is not a requirement.
shoulder_press: Overhead pressing combines elbow extension with raising the arms overhead.
Builds controlled overhead pressing strength through the shoulders and triceps.
First demonstrate the overhead range without weight; use only a range that stays comfortable.
raise: Lateral raises lift the arms to the side against resistance.
Trains shoulder strength through an arm-raising motion with a relatively light load.
Begin with a load that lets the arms move without a bounce from the legs.
rear: Reference supports controlled pulling with a stable torso; rear-delt variants need trainer verification.
Trains the back of the shoulders and the upper back through a controlled pulling arc.
Practise the arm path without weight before adding light resistance.
row: Rows pull a load toward the torso while maintaining a stable starting position.
Builds horizontal pulling strength through the upper back and elbow flexors.
Start light enough to pause briefly at the end of the pull without twisting.
pulldown: Pulldowns draw an overhead resistance toward the upper torso.
Trains the back and arm muscles in a vertical pulling pattern.
Select a resistance or assistance that permits control at both ends of the movement.
pullover: Reference identifies the overhead pulling family; straight-arm mechanics require trainer verification.
Trains bringing the upper arms down toward the torso while keeping elbow movement small.
Use a modest overhead reach rather than forcing a shoulder stretch.
curl: Curls train elbow flexion while the torso remains stable.
Builds elbow-flexor strength with a controlled curl and lowering phase.
Use a light load that does not require a forward shoulder swing.
triceps: Triceps extensions straighten the elbows against resistance.
Trains elbow extension while the shoulder position is kept relatively steady.
First find a comfortable elbow and shoulder position, then add resistance gradually.
squat: Squats bend and extend the knees and hips with the feet supported.
Trains coordinated knee and hip extension in a squat pattern.
Start with a depth that preserves stable foot pressure and controlled movement.
lunge: Lunges load a split stance through knee and hip motion.
Builds leg strength while controlling one side of the body at a time.
Practise a shallow bodyweight version and use a stable support if balance limits control.
hinge: Deadlifts use hip and knee extension to lift a load.
Trains the posterior chain through a hip-hinge pattern with controlled trunk positioning.
Learn the hip movement with a light load; reduce depth before losing your chosen trunk position.
bridge: Bridges raise the pelvis through hip extension.
Builds hip-extension strength with the upper body supported.
Learn to finish with the hips extended without trying to lift the ribs higher.
leg_curl: Reference identifies posterior-chain anatomy only; knee-flexion variant needs trainer verification.
Trains the hamstrings by bending the knee against resistance.
Use a short controlled range initially and increase it only while the pelvis remains steady.
leg_extension: Leg extensions straighten the knees against resistance.
Trains knee-extension strength with the thigh supported.
Adjust the machine to your leg length and choose a comfortable range at light resistance.
hip_side: Reference identifies hip musculature only; side-motion variants need trainer verification.
Trains lateral hip control through a deliberate sideward leg movement.
Keep the movement small enough that the pelvis does not roll or tilt.
calf: Calf raises lift the heel by moving through the ankle.
Builds calf strength through controlled heel raising and lowering.
Begin on a flat surface and use support before adding load or extra depth.
core: Plank variants maintain trunk position against gravity; dynamic variants need trainer verification.
Trains deliberate trunk control while the limbs or external resistance challenge position.
Shorten the lever or movement range so you can maintain position and continue breathing.
grip: Reference establishes forearm involvement in gripping; grip-specific mechanics need trainer verification.
Trains controlled hand, wrist, or forearm force using a supported or carried load.
Use a light load and a comfortable wrist position before increasing resistance.
cardio: Library identifies cardiovascular exercise as a separate training category; machine-specific review required.
Supports rhythmic whole-body activity at an individually chosen effort.
Start slowly and learn the equipment controls before increasing speed or resistance.
